thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: AZ2 inference cluster error-rate spike > 35% (policy: az-gpu-errors-high)

pagerduty: Incident 67291 triggered (severity: P1) — page sent to 'infra-oncall'

raj (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it. hitting the dashboards now.

sara (infra): seeing CPU and GPU driver errors on az2-gpu-*-pod, kernel OOM messages in node logs. rolling tail of the node logs here:
```
Mar 14 03:20:12 host-az2-gpu-12 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 14 03:20:13 host-az2-gpu-12 systemd: docker[4123]: container killed by OOM
```

marta (sre): is autoscaler behaving? could be a bad scaling loop. checking scaling events.

raj (oncall): autoscaler shows many scale-ups then immediate evictions — pods scheduling onto preemptible nodes and getting reclaimed. also saw kube-scheduler backpressure warnings. likely capacity churn.

ryan (platform): confirming — cloud provider reports a transient AZ2 maintenance event that reduced spare capacity. not sure why preemptible usage spiked in our GPU pool. pulling allocation logs.

devex-bot: quick link to alert: https://console.redwood.example/ops/alerts/67291

sara (infra): recommended immediate mitigation: 1) shift new inference traffic off az2 to az3, 2) enable fallback model variant on az1 for critical customers, 3) pause autoscaler for the GPU pool to stop churn.

raj (oncall): doing (1) now — updating routing policy to avoid az2. running command: 
```bash
routectl update-policy --pool inference-prod --avoid-az az2 --priority az3,az1
```

incident-bot: routectl job enqueued (job id 9921).

marta (sre): while that applies, please enable the emergency fallback routing so customer-facing requests go to az3. Use canary=10% then ramp.

raj (oncall): enabling fallback canary 10% -> az3 now.

devex-bot: canary toggled: az3=10% (trace id: c-9921)

sara (infra): pausing autoscaler for gpu-pool-prod to stop noisy scale events: 
```bash
kubectl annotate hpa/gpu-pool-prod autoscaler.paused=true --overwrite
```

ryan (platform): also removing preemptible node template from GPU pool to stop further evictions. doing rolling replacement with standard instances. ETA ~12m.

marta (sre): logging customer impact: we currently see ~28% increase in 5xxs for customers routed to az2 over last 10m. critical customers (acct-88, acct-312) experiencing latency spikes and intermittent failures. notify CS and pages if SLA breach expected.

raj (oncall): posted interim note to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1968123456 — short message and contact.

devex-bot: Automated mitigation check: canary success 10% -> 99% success on az3 after routing shift :white_check_mark:

sara (infra): replacing nodes done for 3/5 worker pools. eviction rate down. GPU driver errors dropping in logs.

marta (sre): rolling up telemetry — request error-rate across region az2 dropped from 35% -> 9% since routing change. still seeing pod restarts but no customer-facing failures for traffic now on az3.

ryan (platform): completed emergency node template swap. all new nodes are non-preemptible. we should leave autoscaler paused until we confirm stability.

raj (oncall): acknowledging. leaving autoscaler paused. will move all active traffic off az2 unless platform calls failover rollback.

marta (sre): can we initiate a controlled failover for pinned customers (acct-88) now rather than wait? they reported degraded UX.

ryan (platform): initiating per-tenant routing move for pinned customers to az3. command: 
```bash
redwoodctl tenant-route promote --tenant acct-88 --target az3 --force
```

incident-bot: Tenant route job queued (job 9937) — will stream progress into thread.

devex-bot: acct-88 route promoted: success. customer notification prepared, pushing to CS. :envelope_with_arrow:

marta (sre): summary for postmortem notes: probable root cause = cloud provider AZ2 capacity maintenance coinciding with preemptible instance usage in our GPU pool -> high eviction -> scheduler churn -> OOMs on nodes -> request error spike. mitigation = routing off az2, swap node template, pause autoscaler, tenant failovers.

raj (oncall): creating incident runbook ticket and linking runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/incident-runbooks/az2-eviction-fallback

sara (infra): recommending follow-ups: 1) audit pool instance templates to avoid preemptible in prod GPU pools; 2) add autoscaler safety (min-stable-time) to avoid immediate re-adds; 3) improve alerting to correlate cloud AZ maintenance with our scaling decisions.

marta (sre): assigning follow-ups to platform and infra leads. I'll start the post-incident doc.

raj (oncall): handing off to oncall-next for monitoring and post-ops. @oncall-next you're up for the next 8h — watch the replay and confirm autoscaler unpause decision. :hand: 

oncall-next: ack — taking over. will keep watch and escalate if error-rate resurges.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident 67291 acknowledged by raj (oncall). status: mitigated -> monitoring.

pagerduty: Incident 67291 — acknowledged. no active escalations.

marta (sre): final note: we've reduced customer impact to acceptable levels, mitigation in place. tagging this thread with postmortem-needed and follow-up-required. closing live page. :heavy_check_mark:

raj (oncall): thanks everyone. logging timeline and saving logs to the incident archive: s3://incidents/1968123456/logs.tar.gz

devex-bot: archived.
